Beállítom Néhány nap alatt legalább hét amerikai államban hajtottak végre kibertámadásokat – vélhetően iráni – hekkerek különböző vízművek ellen, rávilágítva arra, hogy milyen sebezhető az Egyesült Államok kritikus infrastruktúrája, különösen az ivóvíz-szolgáltatás és a szennyvíztisztítás. Az amerikai hatóságok és kibervédelmi szakemberek már évek óta kongatják a vészharangot, hogy különböző külföldi országokhoz köthető hekkerek rendszeresen támadják az amerikai infrastruktúrát, a kisebb vízművek pedig szinte teljesen védtelenek az ilyen akciókkal szemben. Elsőként Minnesota jelezte múlt csütörtökön, hogy nagyjából 36 településen támadták hekkerek a helyi vízműveket, de valójában a támadásokat először négy nappal korábban észlelték. A hét elején aztán az FBI és az EPA környezetvédelmi ügynökség bejelentette, hogy hétfő óta legalább hét államból jelentettek kibertámadásokat. Részleteket nem árultak el, de később Michigan és Dél-Dakota is elismerte, hogy a hekkelések érintik az államaikat. A támadók a vízművek különböző eszközeit működtető és a távoli elérés miatt az internethez is csatlakoztatott, programozható logikai vezérlőket (PLC) célozták, és azokon keresztül tudtak zavart okozni a működésben. Mivel ezeket az eszközöket minden amerikai államban használják, szakértők szerint valószínű, hogy még több állam érintett lehet . A szövetségi kibervédelmi ügynökség (CISA) ideiglenes igazgatója arra biztatta a kritikus infrastruktúrákhoz köthető cégeket, hogy a lehető leggyorsabban kapcsolják le az internetről a PLC-ket és a működéshez szükséges más technológiákat. A szövetségi hatóságok és helyi tisztviselők szerint a támadások miatt sehol sem került veszélybe az ivóvíz minősége, és a legtöbb helyen fennakadások sem voltak, mert gyorsan át tudták állítani kézi vezérlésre az automatizált rendszereket, és lekapcsolták a megtámadott PLC-ket az internetről. A támadók jelszavakat és hálózati beállításokat tudtak megváltoztatni , megakadályozva ezzel egyes eszközök működtetését. A behatolások egyes helyeken nyomáscsökkentést okoztak, ami elvileg azt okozhatja, hogy kezeletlen talajvíz juthat az ivóvízrendszerbe – közölte az FBI . A fő probléma az, hogy ilyen támadásokkal a hekkerek elvileg képesek lehetnek úgy módosítani az ivóvízhez adott vegyi anyagok mennyiségét, hogy az már káros legyen az egészségre, megzavarhatják a szennyvíztisztítást, megakadályozhatják az ivóvíz eljutását az emberekhez, vagy tönkre tudják tenni a szivattyúkat és egyéb eszközöket. Vízműveknél dolgozó szakemberek az NPR-nak nyilatkozva amiatt aggódtak a leginkább, hogy a támadók képesek „vízkalapácsot” , vagyis hirtelen nyomáshullámot létrehozni a nyomás folyamatos változtatásával, ami rengeteg helyen roncsolhatja szét a csöveket. Iránt sejtik a támadások mögött Az eseteket vizsgáló nyomozók szerint iráni hekkerek hajtották végre a támadásokat, de az amerikai hírszerző ügynökségek egyelőre nem tudták teljes bizonyossággal kijelenteni, hogy Irán állt a támadások mögött. Vizsgálják azt a lehetőséget is, hogy a támadók irániaknak álcázták magukat, hogy feszültséget szítsanak az egymással háborúzó Egyesült Államok és Irán között, miközben Washington és legalábbis az iráni rezsim egyes vezetői a megfeneklett béketárgyalások felélesztésén dolgoznak - írta a CBS News . Donald Trump amerikai elnök pénteken kijelentette , nem gondolja, hogy iráni kibertámadás történt Minnesotában, és minden bizonyíték nélkül az állam demokrata vezetését tette felelőssé . „Iránra fogják. Nem hiszem. Szerintem Minnesota tette, mert nagyon alkalmatlanok” – közölte az amerikai elnök, aki szerint „Iránnak nagyobb problémái is vannak, mint Minnesota miatt aggódni”. Az állam kormányzója, a Trump által korruptnak nevezett Tim Walz az X-en reagált az elnök vádjaira. „Trump pontosan tudja, ki a felelős ezért a támadásért, és azt is, hogy más államokat is elértek. Így néz ki a modern hadviselés, és ez ismételten rávilágít arra, hogy nincs terv az Irán elleni háború megnyerésére” – írta Walz, aki Kamala Harris alelnökjelöltje volt a 2024-es elnökválasztáson, és az elmúlt két évben rendszeresen voltak csörtéi Trumppal. Szövetségi tisztviselők Trump kijelentése után magánbeszélgetésekben azt mondták, hogy Irán a legfőbb gyanúsított. Az előzetes vizsgálatok során egyelőre nem találtak perdöntő bizonyítékot, de ez nem szokatlan bonyolult kibernyomozásokban – írta a New York Times . A minnesotai Braham város republikánus polgármestere a lapnak kijelentette, hogy az elnöknek joga van a véleményéhez, de a szövetségi és helyi hatóságok nem kételkednek, és elég biztosak abban, hogy iráni szereplők hajtották végre a támadásokat, csak ezt nyilvánosan még nem merik hangoztatni. Szintén Iránhoz kötötte a támadásokat egy, a Wired magazin birtokába került feljegyzésben, amit az amerikai vízművek kiberbiztonságával foglalkozó WaterISAC nevű iparági csoport küldött szét. A Tenable kiberbiztonsági cég múlt hétfőn közzétett jelentésében azt írták, hogy az amerikai célpontok ellen korábban már több támadást is végrehajtó iráni CybrAv3ngers hekkercsoport állhat az esetek mögött. Donald Trump beszél a 2026. július 31-i kabinetülésen a marylandi Thurmontban – Fotó: Daniel Heuer / Reuters Szakértők szerint az ügyben indított nyomozás be fogja bizonyítani, hogy iráni támadások történtek, mert az ilyen eseteknél „szinte minden első gyanú beigazolódik” – mondta a Timesnak Cynthia Kaiser, aki az FBI egykori magas rangú tisztviselőjeként külföldi kormányokhoz köthető kibertámadások nyomozásait vezette. Szakértők szerint a gyanút erősíti, hogy a támadókat nem a pénzszerzés vezérelte, hanem csak zavart akartak okozni. Irán ráadásul korábban már intézett támadásokat kritikus infrastruktúra, köztük amerikai vízművek ellen, főleg az iráni háború megindítása óta. Veszélyben a védtelen vízművek Az amerikai hatóságok évek óta arra figyelmeztetnek, hogy mennyire sebezhető a kritikus infrastruktúra, amely ellen az elmúlt 15 évben támadások sorát indították orosz, kínai és iráni hekkerek. Két éve kiderült , hogy a kínai államhoz köthető hekkerek ették be magukat a kritikus infrastruktúrába, hogy a megfelelő pillanatban, mondjuk, egy tajvani konfliktus esetén zűrzavart tudjanak okozni. 2024 januárjában orosz hekkerek egy texasi kisváros vízművében okoztak áradást . Az iráni CyberAv3ngers pedig 2023-ban több államban is támadott amerikai vízműveket, míg egy pennsylvaniai kisváros vízművének rendszerében Izrael-ellenes üzenetet küldtek egy monitorra . Az iráni támadások jelentősen megszaporodtak, miután az Egyesült Államok és Izrael február 28-án háborút indított Irán ellen. Márciusban az iráni kormányhoz kötött Handala Hack nevű csapat az orvosi eszközöket gyártó Stryker cég globális működését bénította meg . Az FBI áprilisban közölte , hogy iráni hekkerek az amerikai olaj-, gáz- és vízinfrastruktúrához köthető cégeket támadtak. A szövetségi kibervédelmi ügynökség április elején és július 22-én is figyelmeztetést tett közzé , hogy Iránhoz köthető hekkerek folyamatosan támadják a PLC-ket. A háború kitörése után támadások sorával foglalkoztak, ezek valódi kockázatot jelentenek, és arra számít, hogy folytatódni fognak, mondta a Wirednek áprilisban a Dragos kibervédelmi cég igazgatója, Rob Lee. Nikita Shah, a washingtoni Center for Strategic and International Studies védelmi kutatóintézet kibervédelemmel foglalkozó szakértője a Fortune-nak áprilisban arról beszélt , hogy az amerikai kritikus infrastruktúrát működtető magáncégeknek komolyan kell venniük a fenyegetést. A szakértő szerint az iráni hekkerek a könnyen támadható célpontokra mennek rá, és támadásaik kívülről lehet, hogy hatékonynak tűnnek, de „ha jobban megnézzük, valójában nem különösebben kifinomultak”. Mike Turner republikánus képviselő, a képviselőház hírszerzési bizottságának egykori vezetője vasárnap a CBS Newsnak kijelentette, hogy az Egyesült Államoknak meg kell erősítenie a kritikus infrastruktúra, köztük a vízművek kibervédelmét. Turner szerint az Egyesült Államok ellenségei, mint Oroszország, Kína, Irán és Észak-Korea legitim katonai célpontnak tekintik az infrastruktúrát. Két republikánus képviselő még áprilisban törvénytervezetet nyújtott be a vízművek kiberbiztonságát felügyelő új kormányszerv létrehozására. Az amerikai sajtónak nyilatkozó kibervédelmi szakértők szerint a vízművek különösen könnyű célpontnak számítanak, és a mostani támadásokat is védtelen cégeket keresve hajtották végre. A problémát főleg az okozza , hogy az ivóvízellátást és a szennyvíztisztítást szerte az országban kis helyi cégek biztosítják a településeknek, amik régi eszközöket használnak, nincsenek kibervédelmi szakértőik, sem pedig pénzük arra, hogy végre tudják hajtani a szükséges beruházásokat. A megfelelő kibervédelem több millió dollárba is kerülhet, kiépítése pedig évekig is tarthat. „Ezek általában önkormányzati fenntartásúak, és szűkös költségvetésből működnek. Nincs külön biztonsági személyzet, nincs biztonsági műveleti központ. Sok esetben még eszközleltáruk sincs, amely egyáltalán megmutatná, mi van kitéve a veszélynek” – mondta a Wall Street Journalnek Kurt Gaudette, a Dragos kibervédelmi cég alelnöke. A vízművek közül sok elavult eszközöket használ, és rendszeresen csatlakoztatnak az internethez a működéshez kritikusan fontos rendszereket a távoli elérés biztosítására – sorolta a problémákat Gary Barlet kiberbiztonsági szakértő. Az EPA környezetvédelmi ügynökség 2023-ban egy rendeletben arra utasította az amerikai vízműveket, hogy vizsgálják felül kiberbiztonsági intézkedéseiket és új szabályokat vezetett be. A rendeletet azonban hónapokkal később visszavonták , miután több állam is pert indított. Az EPA 2024 májusában arra figyelmeztetett , hogy jelentős számú helyi vízműnél vannak sebezhető pontok, miközben egyre gyakoribbak és súlyosabbak az azok ellen végrehajtott kibertámadások. A szervezet szerint ellenőreik szerte az országban ijesztő kiberbiztonsági hiányosságokat találtak. Több helyen a gyári jelszavakat használták különböző eszközöknél, ugyanazt a jelszót használta minden dolgozó, vagy nem szüntették meg volt dolgozók hozzáférését a rendszerekhez. A minnesotai Braham polgármestere a New York Timesnak és a Washington Postnak azt ecsetelte, hogy a hozzájuk hasonló kisvárosoknak komoly pénzbeli támogatásra van szükségük a kritikus infrastruktúra védelmének megerősítéséhez. „Az informatikai infrastruktúra korszerűsítése nagyon költséges, mi pedig egy nagyon kis önkormányzat vagyunk” – mondta Nate George. Szerinte az államoknak kéne állniuk a megkövetelt fejlesztések kiépítésének és működtetésének költségeit. Az Egyesült Államokban található több tízezer, egész évben működő vízműnek „kevesebb mint fél százaléka figyel oda a kiberbiztonságra” – mondta a Washington Postnak Joshua Corman, az Institute for Security and Technology nevű kibervédelmi intézet szakértője. Kiemelte, hogy az amerikai vízművek rendkívül sebezhetők. „Eddig is prédának számítottunk, csak éppen nem volt olyan ragadozó, amelyik kifejezetten a vízre ment volna rá, de ennek most vége.” Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! News F16 fighter jets of the Romanian Air Force and the Romania based European F-16 Training Center (EFTC), perform a fly-by at the Black Sea, Defense, Aerospace and Security (BSDA) international exhibition in Bucharest, Romania, Wednesday, May 22, 2024. Associated Press File Photo BUCHAREST, Romania — Since Russia’s full invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the war has repeatedly spilled across Romania's border as drones violate the airspace of the neighboring European Union and NATO member. Now Romania is trying something new to stop the incursions: shooting down the drones. Romanian pilots shot down the first of three drones in as many days from F-16 fighter jets starting Friday as Russia intensified attacks against Ukraine near the border. After determining the drones were of Russian origin, Romania summoned Moscow’s ambassador in protest and expelled a Russian diplomat on Monday. Drones have crossed into Romanian territory multiple times from Ukraine to the north and east, including in May when a drone injured a mother and child after crashing into an apartment block in the eastern town of Galati along the Danube River. Romanian authorities largely responded by scrambling jets, collecting debris, erecting fallout shelters near the border and frequently admonishing Moscow for its war spilling into its territory. Romania and Poland also acquired the MEROPS system , which fires short counter-drones to take down incoming stray drones, following a spate of incursions along NATO’s eastern flank late last year. Drones have crossed into the territories of multiple EU countries , but have been a persistent problem for Romania's leadership in the capital Bucharest. At least 19 have entered Romania’s airspace this year, while there have been 50 cases of drones or drone fragments identified on its territory since the war started in 2022, according to Romania's Ministry of National Defense. Romanian President Nicusor Dan on Sunday congratulated the Romanian pilots for downing the drones and blamed Russia for the incursions. “It is unacceptable and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romanian airspace,” he said. Romania shifts the approach to stray drones Despite passing legislation last year to shoot down drones in its airspace, which was strongly opposed by nationalist political parties, Romania has avoided shooting them down until now. Romanian military analyst Radu Tudor said the May drone incident in Galati may have “changed something in the Romanian authorities’ mentality” in how to approach the issue. “This was somehow a kind of psychological trigger, in order to say: ‘OK, enough is enough,’” Tudor said. “Until now, it probably was an Allied decision in NATO not to respond with firepower, because it was somehow a danger of escalation.” “I think it’s not only a change of attitude of Romania, I think it’s a change of attitude in NATO,” he added. Before the three interceptions over the past week, Romanian pilots also shot down a stray Ukrainian drone above Estonia in May. Romanian pilots and planes are based in Lithuania to provide broad strike capabilities for NATO. “They saw so many signals that Russia is trying to provoke NATO,” Tudor said. “Romania is the only NATO country who shot down four drones on the eastern flank — three on Romania and one in Estonia.” The message sent to Moscow mirrors a statement by NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at the organization's summit in Ankara, Turkey, earlier this month: “‘Don’t play with us’.” Russian diplomat expelled In response to the drone incursions, Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Russia’s ambassador in Bucharest on Monday and presented him with fragments of a drone, saying Moscow “bears exclusive responsibility for all these grave incidents.” The ministry also expelled a member of the Russian mission, who was given five days to leave the country. “The Russian side learned what they already knew: the drones downed on Romanian territory belong to them,” Foreign Minister Oana Toiu wrote in a post on X. “Drone fragments recovered by the Ministry of National Defence and the ongoing prosecutor investigation confirm their Russian origin beyond any doubt.” The Russian embassy in Romania responded in a statement posted on its Facebook page, saying Russia “has never directed and does not direct combat drones” to Romanian territory and denied the allegation as “completely unfounded.” “An unprovoked expulsion of a Russian employee will not go unanswered,” the embassy said. Tactical shift to down errant drones Cristian Popovici, the Romanian defense ministry’s head of public relations and a former air defense officer, said tactics have been developed to eliminate errant drones. “We recorded more than 100 attacks with drones near our border with Ukraine, and many of them resulted in debris or even drones that penetrated our airspace,” he told the Associated Press. “Our pilots and our air force, we developed the tactics, procedures, and now we can face and we can eliminate this threat.” The change began when Romanian pilots shot down a drone over Estonian airspace and from that point the military applied “lessons learned” and had a “100% rate success in three days with three drones,” Popovici said. Despite the new approach to stray drones, Popovici said Romania does not plan to become entangled in the war between Russia and Ukraine. “We are in a peacetime, we are not involved in this fight,” he said. “If Russia wants to escalate with NATO, it’s up to them. I’m not sure it’s a wise move now.” Romania's President Nicusor Dan arrives for the EU summit in Brussels, Thursday, June 18, 2026. https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-could-ex-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5J4z0 Khan has been jailed since 2023 Image: Arif Ali/AFP Advertisement Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be shifted to a private hospital after Khan's family and political supporters repeatedly raised concerns about the 73 year old's deteriorating health in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail. The founder of the opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has been imprisoned since August 2023 and is currently serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges he says are politically motivated. The former prime minister was ousted in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. Khan and his supporters say Pakistan's influential military is trying to keep him out of politics, an allegation the military denies. Despite his remaining behind bars, Khan remains politically popular. Despite a crackdown on the PTI following Khan's arrest, the candidates backed by him performed strongly in the February 2024 elections. "Three years in prison have not removed Khan from Pakistani politics. He remains PTI's biggest political asset, but the party's reliance on him has also exposed weaknesses in its leadership and organization," Raza Rumi, a US-based Pakistani political analyst, told DW. Dousing speculation of a new deal for Khan The transfer of Khan to the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for medical assessment has added a new dimension to the debate over his future and the possibility of political negotiations. However, Khan's adviser Sayed Zulfi Bukhari rejected speculation that court decision was the result of any political deal with the government. "There is no deal between Imran Khan and anyone. This is the Supreme Court's decision, which is very much welcomed," Bukhari said. Pakistan's Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said in a video statement issued on Tuesday night that the government would challenge the Supreme Court order , claiming it was unlawful. The minister said a convicted prisoner must be treated inside the jail or at a public hospital according to law, adding that he was requesting Khan's medical tests be carried out at a government hospital instead of a private facility. "Legally, Khan has not been granted bail nor have his convictions been suspended. He will remain a prisoner, and the hospital executive ward shall serve as a sub-jail. Unfortunately, most ordinary prisoners with far more serious ailments are never allowed such facilities by the courts," Osama Malik, a legal expert, told DW. Pakistan's Minister of State for Interior, Talal Chaudhry, told DW that "Khan's cases will be decided by the courts." Khan's health problems PTI's Bukhari told DW that Khan "hasn't been receiving the right medical care in prison." "That is why it has got to this stage. He has been kept in complete solitude, which has deteriorated his health." Khan's PTI party has said he's suffering from various health conditions , including poor eyesight, fluctuations in blood pressure, and anxiety linked to restricted contact with his family, and has been unable to access specialist medical care. Can Pakistan still help end the US-Iran war? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Some analysts think that the health concerns are now serious enough to have prompted Supreme Court intervention. "Beyond the medical issues, this is also about trust. The PTI and Khan's family have repeatedly questioned his access to doctors and the transparency of his treatment," said analyst Rumi. "After three years in prison, and given his age, any deterioration in his health carries major political consequences. The state, therefore, has every reason to ensure credible and transparent medical care," he added. The court also ordered a medical board, including Khan's sister, Dr. Uzma Khan, and personal physician Dr. Faisal Sultan, to oversee his treatment. The future of Khan and his PTI party Khan's continued imprisonment has tested the PTI's ability to maintain its political strength, and the party's future will depend on whether it can maintain support without the direct political presence of its figurehead. "Khan's political future does not look bright; he will have to compromise his political future. He will remain in jail, and even if his PTI party comes to power in the future, Khan will not be part of the government," Qamar Cheema, a political analyst, told DW. At the same time, Khan's continued popularity makes it difficult for authorities to remove him completely from the political equation in Pakistan . "For the state, the dilemma remains: keeping Khan imprisoned has not neutralized his influence, while releasing him without a broader settlement could revive the confrontation," remarked analyst Rumi. Rumi added that any lasting political settlement with Khan would likely require an understanding with the military establishment, which remains a key stakeholder in Pakistan. "Such a deal could involve legal relief for Khan, greater political space for PTI, and eventually his release, in return for PTI easing its confrontation with the military and pursuing a negotiated political process. But deep mistrust remains a major obstacle, while Khan's reluctance to compromise limits the prospects for a settlement," he said. Analyst Cheema said he doesn't think there is any possibility of a deal between the government and Khan. "This was a genuine understanding in the Supreme Court that he should have been given proper health care," he said. Are Pakistan and Afghanistan heading for war? The Assumption of the Virgin Mary is the patron saint of most monasteries in Romania and because of that the aforementioned holiday is reason for the biggest pilgrimages in this country. Structures with the Romanian Interior Ministry have deployed additional personnel to contribute to public safety in the Romanian Black Sea resorts presently in full holiday season. Their mission is to ensure the public order at the events occasioned by the Navy Day but also to ease road traffic and for rapid intervention in emergency situations. Policemen are present around the worship places as well. DAY Navy Day was celebrated in Romania on Saturday, August 15. The centre of the celebration events was the city of Constanta, on the Black Sea coast, where over 35 hundred Romanian and foreign servicemen participated in the military ceremony and the joint naval drill led by Romania’s Naval Forces. The events were attended by more than 50 ships and vessels, armored amphibious transporters and artillery pieces, belonging to the Navy Forces, Coast Guards, the Romanian Agency of Saving Human Lives at Sea, the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations and Romania’s Air Club. From the allies, two Spanish F-18 fighter jets, which are carrying out NATO’s strengthened air policing missions, and a maritime surveillance plane, Atlantique 2, of the French Navy, also attended the events. A brass-band concert and torchlight procession by the sailors as well as a light and laser show were the final points of the ceremonies on this day. MESSAGES ‘In the past years, the Black Sea has become a crucial area for Europe’s security’ Romanian President, Nicusor Dan, says in his Navy Day address. “The Black Sea is an area where Romania is affirming its strategic interests and projecting its future”, the Head of the Romanian state went on to say. “The Black Sea means trade, energy and connectivity.” “The war in Ukraine proved that Romania is not at the edge of the European Union, Romania is the Union’s first defence line; we are in the Eastern Flank, at the EU’s most important border, the border between a free Europe and a country where citizens are defending their freedom with the price of their lives, and that obliges us,” Romania’s acting Defence Minister says during the ceremonies in Constanta. “It obliges us, Radu Miruta says, because peace is not kept by hoping that others do not attack us, peace is kept by equipping ourselves and making others realize that if they attack us, there will be a heavy price to pay.” “I am here to thank all those who are vigilant on the sea so that we can sleep safe and sound on the ground, to thank all those who support these people, their families, ship builders, port workers, all our partners with whom we cooperate for the security of our eastern border and in the Black Sea”, the acting Prime Minister, Ilie Bolojan says. AMENDMENTS This weekend, the Labour Ministry submitted to the Presidential Administration a series of fresh amendments to the Public Sector Wage Law. President Nicusor Dan has asked for these amendments ahead of a new meeting with the political leaders with a view to reaching an agreement on endorsing and promulgating the law by August 31, the deadline assumed through the PNRR. According to the acting Labour Minister, Dragos Pislaru, the present version has been significantly improved in two areas, healthcare and education. The Minister also says the amendments are targeting the salary scale for high-ranking officials. He says he has received the salary scale by e-mail from the Chamber of Deputies, and that it was agreed upon by the leaders of the political Parliamentary groups. According to him, the interim government cannot amend this proposal. 770 million Euros worth of European funds are hinging on the endorsement of the aforementioned law. PNRR Romania has officially submitted payment request No. 5 under the NRRP, totaling 2.84 billion Euros, the interim Minister of Investments and European Projects, Dragoş Pîslaru has announced. This request covers 75 targets and milestones (21 reforms and 54 investments), comprising a net value of 1.65 billion euros in non-repayable European funds (grants) and 433 million euros in loans. This is the penultimate payment request under the NRRP. With this submission, Romania reaches a 78% absorption rate for the grant component. Romania’s Recovery and Resilience Plan is funded with 21.41 billion euros, consisting of 13.57 billion euros in grants and 7.84 billion in loans. DRONE A drone, which was discovered close to the town of Plauru, Tulcea county, eastern Romania, was neutralized on Saturday by a specialized team from the country’s Defence Ministry. That has been the second drone discovered in Tulcea, after the one in the Macin Mountains. Another drone was discovered close to the stabilopodes in the resort of Costinesti, on the Romanian Black Sea coast, on Thursday. An unprecedented intensity has been reported in the drone attacks on the Ukrainian front, and the Romanian army radars have discovered over 100 drones close to Romania’s airspace in the past 96 hours. Since the onset of the war in Ukraine, drones or parts of drones have been discovered on the Romanian territory in fifty occasions. Scores of airspace violation have been reported in Romania since the beginning of the war. The most severe incident was reported in late May, when a Russian drone crashed into a block of flats in Galati, eastern Romania, wounding two. Romania’s Air forces shot down three drones in July. https://weeklyworker.co.uk/worker/1604/c.text: 08.10.2026 Victim of child rape Issue 1604 Categories: Democracy & State More by: Eddie Ford Cruel and unusual treatment Her botched execution is a gruesome reminder of the utterly barbaric nature of the death penalty, says Eddie Ford. But what about dealing with counterrevolutionaries during a bitterly fought civil war? Christa Pike, the US death row inmate, was “conscious and speaking” on the night of October 6 after surviving two supposedly lethal injections in Tennessee’s Riverbend Maximum Security Institution. Her apparent recovery is described as “medically unprecedented” and, while her prognosis remains unclear, her defence team say that “at a minimum, we expect a long recovery.” They expressed their gratitude that the first responders and the medical team at the hospital “treated Christa like a human”. By contrast, in a display of utter barbarity, Pike remained handcuffed and shackled to her hospital bed, while doctors tried to clear her body of the injected chemicals. Becoming the only person known to have survived a complete execution attempt in the US, there has been widespread revulsion over her botched execution. Frankly, it amounted to nothing more than state torture. On top of all that, she underwent nearly 30 years of solitary confinement on death row. But we now have the appalling possibility, of course, that the authorities might try to kill and torture her again if she recovers sufficiently from the first attempt - whether by injecting pentobarbital once more, or using some other grisly method. Commute sentence Moreover, surely Christa Pike’s sentence should be commuted with a view to her eventual release from prison. Her lawyers have filed for clemency on the basis that her execution would be unjust, given she was just 18 at the time of the crime and her own horrific experiences as a teenager. Bill Lee, governor of Tennessee, has paused all executions in the state for the remainder of the year. Pike, now aged 50, would have been the first woman executed in that state since 1820. She and her boyfriend lured a 19-year-old classmate into woods, where they tortured and killed her. A media frenzy broke out and she was portrayed as evil incarnate. In fact, she herself was a victim who had suffered extreme and violent abuse since she was a child, including being raped by several strangers, as well as beatings by her relatives. Pike was subsequently diagnosed with bipolar and post-traumatic stress disorders. In what was expected to be her final statement, Pike said she loved both her supporters and those who hated her alike. During the execution attempt, according to her lawyers, prison officials tried to start intravenous lines by using at least seven needles on Pike’s arm. “One needle was bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed,” a defence filing states. While receiving the two doses, “she could be heard crying, whimpering and breathing loudly throughout the procedure”, her lawyers said. Under Tennessee’s lethal injection protocol, if the person remains alive five minutes after receiving a first dose of the pentobarbital injection, a second injection is to be administered - but the execution protocol does not say what should happen if the person remains alive after that. This was actually the second failed execution this year in Tennessee involving the same doctor in both cases. When the execution of Tony Carruthers failed, he was then granted a one-year reprieve - after which they will attempt to kill him again. James Crowson, part of Pike’s defence team, says he was not surprised that Tennessee botched its execution attempt, because attorneys had warned that the procedure was dangerous and potentially cruel - a number of defence filings stated quite clearly that she had “compromised” veins. 1 Crowson also said accounts that officials had followed the written protocol, but the execution was badly mishandled, are not necessarily contradictory, for the simple reason that states that impose the death penalty “don’t really include medicine or science in the discussions, when they’re coming up with these protocols”. As a result of this gruesome incident, Tennessee’s top prison official, Frank Strada - the commissioner of the Tennessee department of correction - is stepping down later this month, as this was the fifth failed execution attempt carried out under his watch. The state has launched an independent investigation into what went wrong, as the authorities have not yet offered any explanations, but there is a strong possibility that, apart from being incorrectly administered, the pentobarbital was degraded due to factors including poor manufacturing or improper storage - factors about which experts had previously expressed concern. Grotesque What happened to Christa Pike is a blatant violation of the constitutional prohibition on “cruel and unusual” punishment. Bryan Stevenson, the founder of the Equal Justice Initiative in Montgomery, Alabama, said that it was time to turn around the “threshold question”, so that, instead of asking whether a prisoner deserved to die for the crime committed, the question should be, “Do our governments which tolerate inequality, unreliability and bias deserve to kill?” 2 In a grotesque spectacle, death penalty states are scrambling to find alternatives to the lethal injection, which was supposed to be the ‘humane’ alternative to a firing squad or electric chair - at the time they were portrayed as an ‘improvement’ on hanging in a system disproportionately handing the death penalty to black men. But inevitably, these alternatives turn out to be no better, if not worse. Alabama briefly tried using an ‘experimental’ procedure using nitrogen gas - one that vets refuse to use as a method for the euthanasia of cats and dogs - but it was blocked in June by a federal judge, ruling that it was an example of “cruel and unusual punishment”. Other states have opted for the firing squad, but recent executions this way have been dogged by bullets missing the heart, to the extent that the suggestion has been raised that some of the mis-targeted shots may have been intentional - which would not be surprising. The last time that the US saw a moratorium on executions was in 1972, when the supreme court ruled in the landmark criminal case, Furman v Georgia , that capital punishment was “capricious and arbitrary” and hence violated the eighth and 14th amendments prohibiting cruel and unusual punishment. 3 When Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 at the age of 20, that made her one of the youngest women to receive a death sentence in the US during the post-Furman period. Although the justices did not rule that the death penalty per se was unconstitutional, the Furman decision invalidated the death sentences of nearly 700 people. But the ban was lifted four years later. Paradoxically, calls for a renewed nationwide pause are reaching fever pitch at precisely the time that pressure to carry out executions is also peaking - which was only to be expected, given Donald Trump’s enthusiasm for the death penalty, repeatedly exhorting various states, as well as the federal department of justice, to speed up judicial killings. Last year saw the highest number of US executions (47 across 12 states) in 16 years, via in particular a resurgence of firing squads, despite medical experts condemning them as “excruciating”. But Trump probably regards that as a bonus . Cheerleaders What do Britain’s death-penalty cheerleaders have to say about Christa Pike? 4 This is the pertinent question raised by Maya Foa, head of the human rights charity Reprieve. 5 Restore Britain has promised to hold a binding referendum on the death penalty, Rupert Lowe arguing in PMQs last year that it was needed for cases where “the evil” is “so irredeemable”, and far more importantly, was “far too often perpetrated by someone who should not be in our country to begin with”. 6 Lee Anderson, the totally obnoxious Reform MP and former Labour councillor, is also in favour of a referendum, convinced that the public would vote in favour of the death penalty. Historically, of course, there has always been a baying ‘pro-hanging’ mob amongst the Tory rank and file. Britain abolished the death penalty for murder in 1965 after the outcry that followed a fatal miscarriage of justice, when Timothy Evans was hanged for murdering his wife and daughter - but they were actually both victims of the serial killer, John Christie, who lived downstairs. Ruth Ellis, the last woman executed in the Britain in 1955, was punched, pushed down the stairs and threatened with murder by the man she shot dead outside a now famous London pub - similar to the hideous treatment meted out to the teenage Christa Pike. And there is clear evidence, whatever the right might say, that capital punishment does not deter crime: in 2024, of the eight most violent states in the US measured by the murder rate, seven had the death penalty. But, regardless, in April the US department of justice published a Trumpian death penalty report that brazenly claimed that all methods of execution available to US states are ‘humane’ - a truly sick and perverse finding despite the mountain of evidence to the contrary going back decades. Proponents of capital punishment, like Rupert Lowe, often claim that it will be reserved for the “worst of the worst” mass murderers, but consistent research shows that in reality the death penalty is actually disproportionately reserved for the most vulnerable - including people with mental illness and intellectual disability, or people who cannot afford good lawyers. In fact, people like Timothy Evans and Christa Pike. Tony Blair infamously promised to be “tough on crime and the causes of crime”, but we always knew what he meant by that - dishing out more punishment and punitive treatment. But we have always stressed that crime can only be understood in relation to the given society. As we live in a class society, anti-social crime is mainly a product of alienation, want or resistance - and the ‘justice system’, reflecting the balance of class forces, essentially aims to beat the population into submission. For us, however, the aim must always be rehabilitation - not punishment or revenge, let alone cruelty. In a society of freely associated producers, prisons would be just a memory, something found in history books. Our history As we state in the CPGB Draft programme (3.17. ‘Crime and prison’), under capitalism “property is considered primary; the person merely a form of property”. 7 We know that far too many people are unnecessarily in prison, especially given that a high proportion of prisoners lack basic literacy skills, have mental health issues or suffer from an alcohol or drug problem. Therefore we say that prisoners “must be allowed the maximum opportunity to develop themselves as human beings” and thus “should only be imprisoned within a short distance of their home locality” (if not, families must be given the full cost of travel for visits). Centrally, prison life “must be made as near normal as possible”, like having the right to vote in elections, etc. Of course, here we simply follow in the footsteps of the socialist movement. Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels certainly took it for granted that the death penalty was archaic and had to go. The Socialist International ran aggressive campaigns against the death penalty. In that spirit the programme of the Russian Social Democratic Party demanded the “abolition of the death penalty”. However, and this is important, that was not an absolute position. The party opposed tsarist executions, but refused to tie the hands of the future in dealing with tsarist counterrevolutionaries. Nonetheless, one of the first acts of the Bolshevik government on November 8 was the abolition decree. However, it was restored as an “exceptional measure” during the civil war, but there was always the promise that this would be temporary. Indeed the death penalty was abolished in January 1920 … only to be restored in May 1920 with the outbreak of war with Poland. By the late 1920s expediency had became the norm … and we all know what happened after that.
